title: Urban National Wildlife Refuge Day and the nature close to home
dek: Today is Urban National Wildlife Refuge Day, a good excuse to find the wild places tucked near our cities.
body: Today is Urban National Wildlife Refuge Day. It is a quiet observance, and I only learned about it recently, but I like the idea behind it. It celebrates the protected wild places that sit close to cities where most of us live.

Many people assume they need to drive for hours to see real nature. Often it is much closer. There can be wetlands at the edge of town, marshes near the airport or a stretch of trail along a river where birds stop to rest.
Fall is a lovely time to go looking. The light is softer in the afternoon, the air is starting to change in many places, and a slow walk feels like exactly the right speed for this season.
I find that even an hour in a place like that resets something in me. I come home noticing birds on the power lines and trees changing on my own street, things I walk past every day without seeing.
This week, look up the nearest wildlife refuge or nature preserve to where you live, and plan one slow walk there before October gets busy.
